:rotating_light: ALERT: streaming-tail latency p99 spike detected in eu-prod (svc=streaming-proxy, route=/v1/stream). p95=1.1s p99=6.2s. SLO breach threshold p99>5s. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/streams/streaming-tail?orgId=1&var-region=eu

emma: ack'ing — I'm oncall now, pulling traces. Notified on-call rotation.

ajay: saw this too — customers on SSE show long pauses between chunks, some sockets hanging. Logs show increased 502/504s from proxy->edge.

sasha: adding context: this started ~6821122200, coincides with a traffic spike from realtime-demo tenant. Could be client backpressure causing buffers to pile up.

emma: good call. On prod, p95 for streaming smaller but p99 tail is what matters. Quick checks:
```
# check proxy pod restarts
kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=streaming-proxy -o wide
kubectl -n prod logs deploy/streaming-proxy --since=15m | grep -E "timeout|writev|broken pipe|upstream"
```

devops-bot: Deploy streaming-proxy v2.14.1 rolled at 6821122380 to eu-prod (canary 10%). No automatic rollbacks reported.

kevin: I'm seeing NGINX upstream errors in the logs: "upstream sent too big header" and lots of "writev: connection reset by peer". That matches client drops.

emma: try immediate mitigations: 1) enable fallback routing to dedicated-pool (lower latency but higher cost), 2) scale proxy pool by +3 pods, 3) bump proxy keepalive and write timeout, 4) temporarily increase max-inflight per-tenant for demo tenant. I'll patch runtime config.

ajay: running scaling now: `kubectl scale deploy/streaming-proxy --replicas=12 -n prod`. Also applied an emergency route: `/v1/stream` -> dedicated-pool via policy route-id: emergency-2026-03-15.

sasha: I pushed an nginx tweak to increase proxy_buffer_size and proxy_busy_buffers_size for eu cluster, and increased upstream read timeout from 30s -> 60s.

tenant-support: flagging customers: "realtime-demo" and two enterprise tenants (acme-corp, finstack) reported truncated streams and reconnect spams. Support has opened tickets and SLO-impact estimates.

emma: checking metrics after actions — p99 dropped to ~3.8s after scale + route fallback. Still seeing sporadic stalls for connections that hit older proxy pods.

devops-bot: scaling completed at 6821122410. New replica set healthy.

kevin: I'm tailing proxy logs — write errors dropped 80% but there's one noisy host (stream-proxy-7) with repeated slow writes. Suggest cordon/replace that node or restart the pod.

emma: restarting the problematic pod now: `kubectl delete pod stream-proxy-7 -n prod`.

lior: picking up handoff in 20m. Summary for next oncall: incident started ~6821122200, root cause likely client backpressure + proxy buffer sizing + traffic spike from realtime-demo causing proxy write stalls. Mitigations applied: scaled proxies, route fallback to dedicated-pool, increased timeouts and buffers, restarted bad pod. Current status: p99 ~2.1s, no new customer alerts but tickets open.

emma: adding follow-ups for postmortem: capture request traces for stalled connections, collect tcpdump for any remaining slow socket hosts, evaluate per-tenant pacing rules and streaming keepalive heuristics. Also consider adding a circuit breaker to avoid proxy-level accumulation (max queue per-connection).

tenant-support: FYI, Acme reported 15 user sessions affected during spike, Finstack ~7 sessions. Both clients use web-socket fallback and had automatic reconnect loops (we should rate-limit retries).

lior: marking paging -> on-call-handoff. If anything flares, ping me @lior and I'll escalate. Leaving a short runbook snippet:
```
1) Check streaming p99 dashboard and sample traces
2) Scale streaming-proxy; enable route fallback to dedicated pool
3) Increase proxy buffers/timeouts temporarily
4) Identify noisy tenant, throttle at ingress if needed
5) Replace problematic pod/node
```

emma: thanks team. I'll open the incident ticket and assign postmortem owner. Closing active page but leaving channel open for monitoring. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident note: paging cleared at 6821122440. Incident ID INC-2026-0315-001.
